items.claim: The severity of a server-side request forgery finding comes from the network position and trust the application lends the forged request, not from the request existing at all, so a hunter must show what the server-side fetch reaches that the client origin cannot.
items.body:
The severity of a server-side request forgery finding comes from the network position and trust the application lends the forged request, not from the request existing at all, so a hunter must show what the server-side fetch reaches that the client origin cannot.

HackTricks reference: request forgery csrf and ssrf (https://oreobiscuit.gitbook.io/introduction/bug-bounty-reports-and-articles/request-forgery-csrf-and-ssrf.md)
items.disproof: If the server-side fetch is shown to originate from the attacker's own network position, or to reach nothing the client origin could not already reach itself, the leverage-based impact claim fails.

sources.quote:
5️⃣ Request Forgery (CSRF & SSRF)

Request forgery vulnerabilities pose serious risks by leveraging the trust and capabilities of web applications to perform unauthorized actions.

If an attacker cannot directly contact a target, but the product has access to the target, then the attacker can send a request to the product and have it be forwarded to the target. The request would appear to be coming from the product's system, not the attacker's system.
In general, basic SSRF (when the response is returned to the attacker), is easier to exploit than Blind SSRF in which the attacker has no feedback on whether or not the attack was successful.
